claim: The twelve steps of the run, as the article's headings list them.
quote: 1 · A real, pinned runtime; 2 · Define the mandate; 3 · Store two facts through Ruflo; 4 · Try something outside its permission; 5 · Save an encrypted recovery point; 6 · Approval means stop; 7 · Remove the original workspace; 8 · Restore in a fresh process; 9 · Ask Ruflo what it remembers; 10 · A missing fact stays missing; 11 · Change the saved copy, try again; 12 · What this run proves

claim: The run's acceptance summary (step 12).
quote: exact recall PASS 2/2; ABP denial PASS; deletion that needs approval BLOCKED, checkpoint retained; fresh-process restore PASS; tampered restore BLOCKED; and semantic recall NOT VALIDATED, because embeddings were off.

claim: The three safeguards tested, all of which held.
quote: three safeguards are tested and hold: a request outside the agent's permission is refused, a deletion that needs approval is stopped, and a tampered checkpoint is rejected.

claim: The restored database had the same SHA-256 fingerprint as the one saved.
quote: A brand-new process restores the checkpoint, the restored database has the same SHA-256 fingerprint as the one saved, and Ruflo reads both facts back word for word.

claim: The Agent Behaviour Policy in the run: four rows scoped to the project, with deletion needing approval, and unsupported or ambiguous policies failing closed.
quote: four Agent Behaviour Policy rows, all scoped to the project: write memory, yes; read memory, yes; read history, yes; delete memory, approval. ... "No raw rule overrides. Unsupported or ambiguous policies fail closed."

claim: Only encrypted SGit objects enter the checkpoint store; private keys are kept apart.
quote: Only encrypted SGit bare objects enter the checkpoint store. Private keys remain in a separate private directory.

claim: The proof of concept states its own limits: recall by meaning was not validated; real-world value and reliability are still to validate.
quote: And still to validate: recall by meaning, real-world value, and installation and ongoing reliability.

quote: This is the first time someone outside our own sessions has taken the two ideas we keep arguing for, an encrypted vault as an agent's memory and a behaviour policy beside the prompt, and run them together inside someone else's agent stack, on camera.
